_comment: Safety-gate SLA (#10). PRE-REGISTERED before any candidate is evaluated — the gate reads the threshold from here, never from a CLI flag, so a verdict can't be bargained with after seeing a score. Composite scenario score = 0.4*HO_success + 0.3*(1 - ping_pong_ratio) + 0.3*coverage_norm, worst case = MIN over every (scenario, seed) in the suite. 0.75 ~= 85% of the A3 baseline's composite (~0.90 on the placeholder map): a candidate may trade a little churn for coverage, but must never fall more than 15% below the standards baseline in its single worst scenario.
_registration_note: Suite history, kept deliberately as the audit trail. v1 (seeds 300-302) re-seeded to 1000+ before any gating after review caught a potential train/eval collision. v1's first run (log 09:08-09:25Z) produced INVERTED verdicts, exposing a scoring defect: the zero-attempt success term (flat 0.5) punished correct restraint in stationary_clusters, rejecting clean candidates at 0.7456 while a weak poison passed. v2 fixed the scoring (zero-attempt success = coverage-conditioned). Round-2 under v2 (log 10:59-11:21Z) promoted the CLEAN candidates correctly but ALSO promoted the poisoned ones: a single reward-flipped client out of three is diluted 1/3 by FedAvg and never crosses the threshold (poisoned-fedavg worst 0.8109 vs clean 0.8730 - degraded, not broken). The threat model, NOT the gate, was too weak. Fix (attacker only; threshold and scoring unchanged): the poisoned client now also BOOSTS its update (model-replacement, --boost ~n_clients) so it survives averaging - the standard strong FL attack that FedAvg fails and coordinate-median resists. Round-3 is the acceptance run. Threshold has been 0.75 throughout; only the adversary strength (the --poison knob issue #9 exposes) changed.
